question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` as an opt-in workspace boundary for default child subagents, or keep explicit child agent profiles plus `requireAgentId` as the supported isolation model?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the requested key is missing, but choosing whether to add a public workspace-access config surface is a security/product boundary decision.

options.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
options.body: Preserve the current model where isolation uses configured child agent profiles plus `requireAgentId`, with docs or diagnostics improvements if maintainers want lower setup friction.

options.title: Add Narrow Opt-In Config
options.body: Implement `subagents.workspace` for same-agent default children only, with strict schema/docs, doctor/security review, and regression coverage across the spawn paths.

options.title: Defer To Broader Workdir Design
options.body: Hold this until workspace, task `cwd`, sandbox policy, and skill workdir isolation are designed together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
recommendation.body: Preserve the current model where isolation uses configured child agent profiles plus `requireAgentId`, with docs or diagnostics improvements if maintainers want lower setup friction.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent security-boundary and spawned workspace override work makes this the closest available routing owner for the public config decision.
